active_product_bottleneck.observation: Draft fused ABI3 checkpoint #662 passes authentic installed Q6/Q64 research transfer versus v0.30.0 (#665/#669: 4.94–49.11x on heterogeneous small-owner Q6/Q64), but early Q1 is 2.13–2.66x slower and one exact-source 262k run crosses the fixed +5%/+3ms veto. #672 proves cached checkpoints can return wrong bytes after public in-memory reference mutation. #676 seals that specific flaw on three hosts but slows all 12 paired cases in two runs by 13–24%; #679 C-fused freeze and #682 tuple-first admission fail their prospective economic tests. All remain unmerged.
active_product_bottleneck.next_discriminator: Apply mandatory frame review: no nearby tuple/list/freeze microvariant without new information. Resolve authenticated reference ownership, exposed API, mutable generation replay and native ABI in one source- and semantics-exact design proof before implementation; price published-Q1, safeguarded-Q6/Q64, cold-open/RSS, recovery, and hostile mutation together. Alternatively move capacity to already-owned P0 correctness integration rather than another speculative Reader patch.

primary_question.hypothesis: A representation/ownership boundary could preserve the demonstrated batched-range acceleration and exact signed-reference semantics without postvalidation O(N) freezing cost or stale mutable checkpoints; it must coexist with current native validator, transaction journal and public Reader descriptors.
primary_question.kill: Any wrong byte under admissible metadata mutation, weakening hostile admission or generation recovery, breaking documented public semantics, unbounded RSS/decode work, or material early-Q1 published-release regression vetoes promotion. #679/#682 already retire the two narrow copy/tuple hypotheses; a further nearby mechanism without new causal evidence is not justified.
evidence: J24C14 #665, J24C15 #669: signed installed Reader Q6/Q64 positive (4.94–49.11x on measured small-owner regimes), early Q1 2.13–2.66x slower; runs 40675424786 / 40675417832 and complete result dossier. Scope excludes large real CDC owners.
J24C16 #672 installed signed in-memory descriptor mutation yields wrong bytes on #662; run 40683558265. Not a malicious-on-disk archive claim.

J24C17 #676 contains that precise mutation on 3 hosts, but two direct economic runs 40692132713 / 40692140648 show +13–24% full-session cost and exposed list-to-tuple API risk. Cannot claim performance product floor.

J24C18 #679 3-host C-fused freeze loses vs CPython tuple (run 40701073699). J24C19 #682 tuple-first decoding fails 3/4 large prospective >5% improvement cases (run 40709133246), incompatible with PyList_CheckExact and mutable journal. Do not repeat threshold gardening.

saturated_families.reason: The existing executor is decision-complete; only execution can change the primary science.
PR #154 measured the duplicate-compression owner and merged PR #155 already productized bounded exact-length reuse in current v0.30.
Current ML is a real byte winner; the completed optimistic lower bound remains 175,333 B below the accepted v0.29 floor, so this proof cannot fire on the row.
A deterministic held-out structural hostile reverses level-6 versus level-19 ordering and preserves a valid exact hierarchical win.

PR #205 retained major Office byte savings but final create remained 1.330773x > 1.25 after multiple materially different rehabilitation attempts; the current family is retired pending a new mechanism.

O210 microbench looked 2.26-11.95x compelling, but authentic O211 #555 measured only 4.4482% full-export CPU at 32 reusable members, below preregistered 5% decision threshold; reopen only if realistic mix changes materiality.

O216 #570 authentic controlled alternative ~4x faster still left +5.34ms/+21.36ms at 65,536/262,144 references versus intentionally unsafe timing floor; do not repeat nearby Python per-ref variants without new architecture.

J24C17 #676 contains mutation but incurs +13–24% full-session cost; J24C18 #679 per-element native construction loses to CPython tuple; J24C19 #682 tuple-first MessagePack misses 3/4 frozen economic gates and conflicts with native Python list/journal ABI. Reopen only on a genuinely different end-to-end ownership model.
J24G16 #681 runs 6.3756x CPU on normal 10k-map metadata, despite saving ~36.6MiB only by refusing over-budget inputs. #684 moved question to native token admission; stop Python threshold variants.

A16-O0/O1 #683 improves decode component but misses 1% full-byte criterion against compact fixed chunk and incurs 7.855x storage regression with incompatible co-owner sets. Avoid more friendly synthetic variants.
